# Table

A table that always uses tabular numbers and shows an empty state when there is no data. Inside a card or
similar container, combine it with the `flush` prop of Panel so that the table sits flush with the edges.

**Category**: Data · **Common uses**: Structured data such as projects, members and activity logs; sortable and paginated

## Import

```ts
import { Table } from 'vellum-ui'
```

## Basic usage

Statuses use Pill, the member column uses Avatar and Text; inside a Panel, add `flush` so the table reaches the
edges.

```tsx
export function Basic() {
  return (
    <Panel flush>
      <Table
        rowKey="id"
        pagination={false}
        dataSource={[
          { id: '1', name: 'Alex Morgan', status: 'active' },
          { id: '2', name: 'Sam Lee', status: 'inactive' },
        ]}
        columns={[
          {
            title: 'Name',
            dataIndex: 'name',
            render: (n: string) => (
              <Inline gap={2}>
                <Avatar name={n} size={20} />
                <Text size="sm" truncate>
                  {n}
                </Text>
              </Inline>
            ),
          },
          {
            title: 'Status',
            dataIndex: 'status',
            render: (s: string) =>
              s === 'active' ? (
                <Pill tone="success" dot>
                  Active
                </Pill>
              ) : (
                <Pill dot>Disabled</Pill>
              ),
          },
        ]}
      />
    </Panel>
  )
}
```

## States

### No data

An empty state is shown automatically when there is no data.

```tsx
export function Empty() {
  return (
    <Panel flush>
      <Table rowKey="id" dataSource={[]} columns={[{ title: 'Name', dataIndex: 'name' }]} />
    </Panel>
  )
}
```

## Props

No props of its own.

Also accepts the props of the corresponding Ant Design component (`TableProps`), except `style` and `className`.

Does not accept `style` or `className`: appearance is adjusted only through the semantic props above and the theme.
